title: K.I.N.D. Fund Scholarships Build Brighter Futures in Malawi
text_paragraph_1: As young learners head back to school this fall, The K.I.N.D. (Kids in Need of Desks) Fund will be making an impact in Malawi, continuing its 16-year mission to outfit classrooms with desks and provide scholarships to help students like Joyce Chisale fulfill their dreams.
text_paragraph_2: In her first year at St. Michaels Girls Secondary School in Mangochi, Malawi, Joyce Chisale got the highest marks in everything from Chichewa language classes to biology and history. But her parents had trouble keeping up with payments; the boarding school's annual fees were roughly half her father's yearly salary, and there were three other siblings to support.
text_paragraph_3: That might have meant the abrupt end of Joyce's formal education and her dreams of becoming a doctor or scientist. Then The K.I.N.D. (Kids in Need of Desks) Fund stepped in, awarding Joyce a full, merit-based scholarship. She went on to complete high school and graduated at the top of her class.

Helios and UNICEF aim to enhance digital learning access in Africa
text_paragraph_1: Helios Towers, a telecommunications infrastructure company, and child rights organisation UNICEF (the United Nations Children’s Fund) have announced a multi-year partnership to expand internet connectivity and digital learning access for children and young people across Africa.
text_paragraph_2: The partnership supports two flagship UNICEF initiatives: Giga, a partnership between UNICEF and the International Telecommunication Union working to connect every school in the world to the internet by 2030, and Learning Passport, which provides localised, high-quality digital learning and skills for children, young people and teachers to continue learning anywhere, at any time, both online and offline.
text_paragraph_3: The partnership will combine Helios Towers’ telecommunications infrastructure expertise with UNICEF’s global leadership in digital inclusion to help connect schools and expand access to quality education in underserved communities.

UNESCO collaborates with Tanzania National Commission to promote youth skills and innovation
text_paragraph_1: Young people from across Tanzania showcased their practical skills, creativity and innovation at the WorldSkills Tanzania National Skills Competition 2026, which received support from the UNESCO Dar es Salaam Office. The competition formed part of the National Education, Skills and Innovation Week, organized by the Ministry of Education, Science and Technology. During the week, UNESCO collaborated with the Tanzania National Commission for UNESCO (NATCOM) to showcase their programmes and activities.
text_paragraph_2: The competition was organized by the Ministry of Education, Science and Technology in collaboration with the National Council for Technical and Vocational Education and Training (NACTVET) and other education and skills-development stakeholders.
text_paragraph_3: The week concluded on 24 August 2026 with a closing ceremony officiated by the Prime Minister of the United Republic of Tanzania, Hon. Dr Mwigulu Lameck Nchemba, at the grounds of Usagara Secondary School in Tanga.

West and Central Africa
text_paragraph_1: The West and Central Africa region is the epicentre of a fast-growing crisis with unprecedented levels of armed violence and insecurity. Millions of people are being driven to the fringes of survival due to the confluence of conflict, deep poverty, demographic pressures, urbanization, weak governance, chronically high food insecurity and malnutrition, and the impact of climate change.
text_paragraph_2: OCHA focuses on strengthening humanitarian coordination and response preparedness through its country offices and its Regional Office for West and Central Africa (ROWCA), which has been based in Dakar, Senegal, since November 2003.
text_paragraph_3: To mitigate the impact of natural disasters and other emergencies, ROWCA works closely with UN Resident Coordinators, Humanitarian Country Teams, national and regional organizations, and Member States.
